nl.statement: finite-population design-based randomization world: a finite unit type `V` with a known directed interference graph (self-loops allowed) and the unit-level product Bernoulli assignment law on `Ω = V → Bool`, carried by `FiniteDesign` with the finite-sum `E`/`Var`/`Cov` algebra. — This is the single highest-leverage reuse decision: the paper's only randomness is the unit-level product Bernoulli assignment, which is exactly `bernoulliDesign p hp0 hp1 : FiniteDesign (V → Bool)` (constant `p i = p`). Cross-coordinate independence — the engine of every orthogonality, block-independence and variance computation in the paper — is then STRUCTURAL (`prodDesign`), not an assumption: `FiniteDesign.E_prod_apply`, `E_prod_apply₂`, `Cov_prod_apply_of_ne`, `Var_prod_apply`, `Var_prod_linear_comb` (ProductVariance) and the block generalizations `E_prod_block_mul`, `Cov_prod_disjoint_zero` (ProductBlock) give the disjoint-block factorization the complete-directed-block arguments need. `\mathbb E_Z` is `FiniteDesign.E` of this design; `P_Z` is the design itself. The graph is a plain `V → V → Prop` with `DecidablePred`, neighborhoods `N i : Finset V`; Causalean's `DAG` is NOT usable (self-loops are required and counted in both degrees), recorded as bypass-justified.

fixed-potential-outcome (noiseless) low-order polynomial interference world: a coefficient schedule `c : (i : V) → Finset V → ℝ` supported on subsets of `N i` of size ≤ β, the induced potential outcome `Y i z = ∑_{S ⊆ N i} c i S ∏_{j ∈ S} z j`, the observed outcome `Y i Z`, the finite-population TTE contrast, and the two model classes (ℓ¹ coefficient-mass and uniformly bounded-outcome). — Search trace: read `../doc/API.md` §18 `Experimentation/` (grepped '^## ' index, then the DesignBased/ExposureMappingInterference/TwoStageInterference/UnknownInterference tables in full); scanned `Causalean/Experimentation/DesignBased/{PotentialOutcome,Exposure,Estimators,HT/*}.lean` for 'potential outcome', 'exposure mapping', 'polynomial interference', 'low order', 'coefficient schedule'; scanned `Causalean/Experimentation/UnknownInterference/Basic.lean` for the whole-assignment PO type. Result: not found — Causalean's design-based PO layers are exposure-mapping-valued (`ProperlySpecified : ∀ i z, yr i z = y i (expo i z)`, `Yobs y f θ i z = y i (expo i z)`, an ABSTRACT finite exposure `θ`) or fully unstructured (`UnknownInterference.y i z`); neither carries the RAW-MONOMIAL POLYNOMIAL structure `Y i z = ∑_{S ⊆ N i} c i S ∏_{j∈S} z j` that every result here is about (the coefficient schedule `c` IS the model parameter, the interaction order β is the model complexity, and the ℓ¹ coefficient-mass envelope is a class restriction on `c`). Bypass-justified: the exposure layer is at the wrong abstraction (it hides the coefficients we must vary). The bridge fact that this PO factors through `z` restricted to `N i` is recorded and proved locally (one lemma), so `DesignBased.PotentialOutcome.ProperlySpecified` remains available as an instance if a later artifact wants it.

design-based decision-theoretic world: GRAPH-AWARE estimators measurable in the full observed data `(G, Z, (Y_i^obs))`, their design mean squared error at a fixed model, the worst case over a model class, and the minimax (inf over estimators) risk. — REVISED (round 2, FLAG-world-arity): an estimator is GRAPH-AWARE — `Estimator V := (V → V → Bool) → (V → Bool) → (V → ℝ) → ℝ` (known graph, assignment, observed outcome vector), matching the core's `\widehat\tau_n` symbol (`refs: [G_n, Z, Y_i^{obs}]`) and def:minimax-risk's 'measurable in `(G_n, Z, {Y_i^obs})`'. The graph is NOT fixed inside the risk functional: `riskAt` COMPOSES the single global estimator with the model's own graph, `riskAt p M est = (bernoulliDesign …).mse (fun z => est (edgeFn M) z (obsOutcome M z)) (tte M)`, where `edgeFn M := fun j i => decide (M.edge j i)` uses the class structure's existing `decEdge` field. The inf–sup is therefore the core's: ONE estimator faces every `(G_n, c)` in the class, and `snipeEstimator β p : Estimator V` (which reads its neighborhoods off its graph argument) is one admissible global competitor, so the middle term of thm:bounded-outcome-degree-frontier is literally `worstRisk … (snipeClipped B β p)`. The per-model risk is exactly `D.mse est μ = D.E (fun z => (est z - μ)^2)` with `D = bernoulliDesign`, `μ = τ_n`; `mse_eq_var_add_bias_sq`, `mse_eq_var_of_unbiased`, `var_le_mse`, `Unbiased` are all reused verbatim (the unclipped-SNIPE branch is `mse = Var` after unbiasedness; the clipping branch uses `mse_nonneg` + a pointwise projection bound). Measurability is vacuous on the finite assignment space and is imposed only on the outcome argument, and only in the converse. `worstRisk`/`minimaxRisk` are `sSup`/`sInf` over the model class / estimator class (build-inline, see def:minimax-risk). Surveyed and bypass-justified: `Causalean.Experimentation.DesignBased.worstRisk` / `IsMinimaxOn` (Optimality/Minimax.lean) minimize over DESIGNS at a fixed estimator, not over ESTIMATORS at a fixed design — the wrong quantifier order for this paper; `ProbabilityTheory.minimaxRisk` (Mathlib Decision/Risk) is kernel/loss-shaped over a general `Kernel`-valued experiment and would force a measure-theoretic re-encoding of the finite design.

least-favourable block world: complete directed `d`-blocks with loops, the block Bernoulli score/energy/representer, the continuous cosine-squared block baseline prior, and the two prior-predictive laws on `({0,1}^V) × ℝ^m` (counting ⊗ Lebesgue) used for the Le Cam converse. — REVISED (round 3, FLAG-finite-mixture) on top of round 2 (FLAG-reuse-precondition). GENERIC Le Cam reuse is RETAINED and unchanged: `Causalean.Stat.tvDist`, `one_sub_tvDist_le_test`, `one_sub_tvDist_le_error_sum`, `real_two_point_lower_bound`, `two_point_lower_bound_of_tvDist_le` (TotalVariation.lean / LeCam.lean / MinimaxRisk.lean) — none of these has an absolute-continuity premise, and none of them requires a finite hypothesis index. DROPPED in round 3: `Causalean.Stat.mixtureReal_le` (Minimax/Mixture.lean), which the round-2 plan cited for the PRIOR REALIZABILITY step. Verified against the source (`Grep 'mixtureReal' ../Causalean/Stat/Minimax/` → `Mixture.lean:53 theorem mixtureReal_le (w : ι → ℝ≥0∞) (hw : ∑ i, w i = 1) …` with `[Fintype ι]`): it is a `.real`-MASS domination bound for a FINITE `Fintype`-indexed convex combination of measures, whereas the baseline prior here is the CONTINUOUS product `⊗_{b ≤ m} f_s(u)du` over `U : Fin m → ℝ` (a compactly supported cosine-squared density, not a finite weight vector), and the quantity to be dominated is an integrated RISK, not a set mass. It cannot discharge the realizability step and the whole `Causalean.Stat.Minimax.Mixture` module is therefore removed from this S-block's modules. REPLACEMENT (local, `small`, built in `Helpers/LeastFavourable.lean` — see def:block-family for the same text): (R0) `prior_integrated_risk_le_worstRisk` — for an admissible estimator `est` (the `AdmissibleEstimator` predicate of def:minimax-risk already carries `BddAbove {riskAt p M est | M}` and outcome-measurability), `∫ riskAt p (blockSchedule σ U) est ∂(blockBaselinePrior s m) ≤ worstRisk p est`. Proof is the ordinary continuous-prior `∫ ≤ sup`: the admissibility lemma of def:block-family puts `blockSchedule σ U` in `ModelClass V d β B` for EVERY `U` in the support, so `riskAt p (blockSchedule σ U) est ≤ worstRisk p est` pointwise by the reused API lemma `le_worstRisk`; then `MeasureTheory.integral_mono_ae` against the constant plus `integral_const` and `IsProbabilityMeasure` (`∫ f_s = 1` is the closed-form `intervalIntegral` computation already needed for (C2), lifted to the product prior by `MeasureTheory.Measure.pi` + `MeasureTheory.isProbabilityMeasure_pi`). Integrability is NOT assumed away: `0 ≤ riskAt ≤ worstRisk` (from `mse_nonneg` and `le_worstRisk`) gives a two-sided bound, and measurability in `U` holds because `riskAt` is a FINITE sum over the finite assignment space of terms polynomial in `U` composed with the outcome-measurable `est`, so `Integrable` follows from `Measure.integrable_of_bounded`-style reasoning on a probability measure. Search trace for a reusable form: `lean_local_search 'mixtureReal_le'` → EMPTY in the index; `lean_local_search 'bayesRisk'` → only `ProbabilityTheory.bayesRisk*` (Mathlib Decision/Risk), which is `Kernel`-shaped over an abstract experiment and would force a measure-theoretic re-encoding of the finite design (same rejection as in def:minimax-risk); `Grep 'integral_mono|Bayes' ../Causalean/Stat/Minimax/` → no integrated-risk-vs-worst-case-risk lemma. Not found ⇒ local, build-inline (three lines of Mathlib `integral_mono_ae`). DROPPED in round 2, and why: the round-1 plan routed the converse through `Causalean.Stat.sq_bhattacharyya_le_two_mul_integral_min` + `Causalean.Stat.integral_min_le_one_sub_tvDist` (BretagnolleHuber.lean), but BOTH are stated for `P₊ ≪ P₋` (they are RN-derivative statements, `∫ √(dP₊/dP₋) dP₋`). The two prior-predictive laws here are mixtures of COMPACTLY SUPPORTED translated cosine-square densities whose supports are non-nested, so `P₊ ≪ P₋` FAILS and those lemmas are unusable; `Pinsker.lean` / `ChiSquared.lean` are excluded for the same reason (KL and χ² are infinite here), as the core's `technical_internal_limitation` records. REPLACEMENT (built locally in `Helpers/HellingerAffinity.lean`, all statements phrased against a COMMON DOMINATING measure `λ = count(V → Bool) ⊗ volume^m`, never against a mutual RN derivative): (C0) `tvDist_le_sqrt_two_mul_one_sub_affinity` — for `P = λ.withDensity f`, `Q = λ.withDensity g` with `f, g ≥ 0` integrable densities of total mass one, `tvDist P Q ≤ √(2·(1 − ∫ √(f·g) ∂λ))`. Proof, both halves elementary and premise-free: `|P.real A − Q.real A| = |∫_A (f − g) ∂λ| ≤ ½∫|f − g| ∂λ` by REUSING `Causalean.Stat.abs_setIntegral_le_half_integral_abs_of_integral_eq_zero` (Scheffe.lean — verified generic: it takes only `Integrable f ν` and `∫ f = 0`, NO `≪`), pushed through `MeasureTheory.withDensity_apply` and `sSup` to bound `tvDist`; then the Cauchy–Schwarz factorization `∫|f−g| = ∫|√f−√g|·(√f+√g) ≤ √(∫(√f−√g)²)·√(∫(√f+√g)²) ≤ 2√(∫(√f−√g)²)` with `∫(√f−√g)² = 2(1 − ∫√(fg))`. This is exactly the paper's own step (`‖P₊−P₋‖_TV ≤ H`, 'Cauchy–Schwarz applied to the densities'), so no fidelity is lost: `H² ≤ 1/4 ⇒ tvDist ≤ 1/2`. (C1) affinity TENSORIZATION for the explicit product density: `∫ √(∏_b f_b · ∏_b g_b) ∂(λ₀ ⊗ volume^m) = ∏_b ∫ √(f_b g_b)`, by `Real.sqrt_mul` on the pointwise product followed by Fubini on `MeasureTheory.Measure.pi` (`integral_finset_prod`-style), with the shared DISCRETE assignment coordinate handled by summing over `z` first (blocks are conditionally independent given `Z`, and the law of `Z` is itself a product over blocks); combined with `1 − ∏ a_b ≤ ∑ (1 − a_b)` for `a_b ∈ [0,1]`. (C2) unchanged: the cosine-squared translation affinity bound `1 − ∫ √(f_s(u−a) f_s(u−b)) du ≤ C(a−b)²/s²`, a closed-form `intervalIntegral` computation (product-to-sum on `cos·cos` over the overlap). NOTE the direction of travel: nothing is now needed ABOUT a Hellinger distance object — only the affinity number `∫√(fg)`, so no general Hellinger theory is built and no `≪` ever appears.

block-local Riesz world: the polynomial subspace `P_d ⊆ L²(P_Z)` spanned by raw monomials of degree ≤ β̄_d on one `d`-block, the all-one-versus-all-zero contrast functional `L_d`, and the fixed-complete-block sequence `(n_t, d_t, G_t)` carrying the block-local linear design-unbiased estimator class. — Search trace: `lean_local_search` for 'Riesz', 'representer', 'L2Space', 'inner product design', 'polynomial space'; read `../doc/API.md` §18 (DesignBased substrate tables) and §10g `Mathlib/SemiInnerProjection.lean`, §10f `Mathlib/FWL.lean`. Result: not found for a design-based `L²(P_Z)` inner-product layer. Bypass-justified and DELIBERATE: `L²(P_Z)` here is the FINITE-dimensional space of functions `(V_b → Bool) → ℝ` with the design inner product `⟪f,g⟫ = D.E (f·g)`, so the whole Riesz story is `Finset` algebra over `FiniteDesign.E`/`Cov` (no Mathlib `L2Space`, no `MeasureTheory` needed); `P_d` is a `Submodule ℝ ((V_b → Bool) → ℝ)` spanned by raw monomials, and orthogonal decomposition `w = g_d + u`, `u ⊥ P_d`, is finite-dimensional projection. The programs `PerturbProg`/`WeightProg` are `sInf` over the feasible sets, with their minimizers identified in lem:block-energy-representer. The only genuinely non-elementary piece is the non-necessity witness, which needs `dim P_{d_t} = ∑_{r ≤ β} C(d_t,r) < 2^{d_t}` for large `d_t` — the centered-monomial family is orthogonal (hence independent) under the product Bernoulli design, so this is a `Finset.card` computation plus `Module.finrank` of the full function space; `Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Dimension` + `Submodule.exists_mem_ne_zero_of_finrank_lt` style reasoning covers it.
\(Z_j\) are mutually independent and \(\Pr(Z_j=1)=p\) for every \(j\in V_n\).
nl.frozen_body:
Let \(V_n\) be a finite population of \(n:=|V_n|\) units, indexed by \(i,j\in V_n\), and let \(p\in(0,1)\). For every unit \(j\in V_n\),
\[
\Pr(Z_j=1)=p,
\]
and the variables \(\{Z_j:j\in V_n\}\) are mutually independent. The assignment law \(P_Z\) on \(\{0,1\}^{V_n}\) is
\[
P_Z(z)
=
\prod_{j\in V_n} p^{z_j}(1-p)^{1-z_j},
\]
and \(\mathbb E_Z\) denotes expectation under \(P_Z\).

review.note: Equality with bernoulliDesign gives exactly the product law of mutually independent Bool-valued coordinates with common treatment probability p; 0 < p < 1 is the declared standing domain of p.

standard.name: unit-level Bernoulli randomization
standard.citation: Mayleen Cortez-Rodriguez, Matthew Eichhorn, and Christina Lee Yu. Exploiting neighborhood interference with low order interactions under unit randomized design. \emph{Journal of Causal Inference}, 11(1):20220051, 2023. arXiv:2208.05553. Theorems 1--2, Equation (4.4), Appendix B, and Section 7.

nl.statement: Self-loops are allowed and count in both degrees, with \(\max_{i\in V_n}|N_i|\le d\) and \(\max_{j\in V_n}|\{i\in V_n:j\in N_i\}|\le d\).
nl.frozen_body:
Let \(G_n\subseteq V_n\times V_n\) be a directed interference graph, and write \(N_i:=\{j\in V_n:(j,i)\in G_n\}\) for the interference neighborhood of unit \(i\). Self-loops are allowed and count in both the in-degree and out-degree. The interference neighborhoods \(N_i\) satisfy
\[
\max_{i\in V_n}|N_i|\le d
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\max_{j\in V_n}\bigl|\{i\in V_n:j\in N_i\}\bigr|\le d .
\]

review.note: Unfolding nbhd and outNbhd gives respectively {j : G j i} and {i : G j i}; their cardinality bounds are exactly the stated in- and out-degree bounds, and no filter removes self-loops.

nl.statement: Set \(\bar\beta_d:=\min\{\beta,d\}\) for every \(d\ge0\); in particular \(\bar\beta_0=0\). If \(\bar\beta_d\ge1\), set \(k_\star(d,\beta,p):=\max\{r\in\{1,\ldots,\bar\beta_d\}:\Delta_r(p)\ne0\}\); since \(\Delta_1(p)=1\), this index set contains \(r=1\), so its maximum is well defined. When \(\bar\beta_d=0\), equivalently \(d=0\) or \(\beta=0\), set \(k_\star(d,\beta,p):=0\) as a totality convention only, never as an attained interaction order. Thus the maximum case applies exactly when both \(d\ge1\) and \(\beta\ge1\); every statement below fixes \(\beta\ge1\).
nl.frozen_body:
For \(r\ge1\), define the order-\(r\) all-one-versus-all-zero Bernoulli contrast coefficient by
\[
\Delta_r(p):=(1-p)^r-(-p)^r .
\]
For every \(d\ge0\), define
\[
\bar\beta_d:=\min\{\beta,d\}.
\]
In particular,
\[
\bar\beta_0=0 .
\]
If \(\bar\beta_d\ge1\), define
\[
k_\star(d,\beta,p)
:=
\max\bigl\{r\in\{1,\ldots,\bar\beta_d\}:\Delta_r(p)\ne0\bigr\}.
\]
Since \(\Delta_1(p)=1\), this maximum is well defined. If \(\bar\beta_d=0\), equivalently \(d=0\) or \(\beta=0\), define
\[
k_\star(d,\beta,p):=0
\]
as a totality convention, rather than as an attained interaction order. Thus the maximum case applies exactly when \(d\ge1\) and \(\beta\ge1\); subsequent statements take \(\beta\ge1\).

review.note: Unfolding effBeta and bernoulliContrast, the filtered interval is exactly {r ∈ {1,…,min β d} : Δ_r(p) ≠ 0}; Δ₁(p)=1 makes it nonempty precisely when min β d ≥ 1, while the empty case returns 0.

nl.statement: Set \(\binom{0}{0}:=1\), \(g_0:=0\), and \(A_0:=0\). Interpret sums over nonempty subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,0\}\) as zero; its assignment space has one empty vector and the empty product equals one. Set \(h_0:=0\) only as an empty-object convention, and never interpret it as \(g_0/A_0\).

For every \(\beta\in\mathbb N\) and \(p\in\mathbb R\), the degree-zero conventions are
\[
\bar\beta_0=0,
\qquad
k_\star(0,\beta,p)=0,
\qquad
g_0=0,
\qquad
A_0=0,
\qquad
h_0=0,
\qquad
h_{0,T}=0\ \text{for every }T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,0\}.
\]
Here \(h_0\) is imposed directly as the zero representer, rather than formed as the quotient \(g_0/A_0\).

nl.frozen_body:
For a coefficient schedule \(c\) and an assignment \(z\in\{0,1\}^{V_n}\), the potential outcome of unit \(i\in V_n\) is
\[
Y_i(z)
:=
\sum_{S\subseteq N_i} c_{i,S}\prod_{j\in S} z_j .
\]
Evaluating the schedule at the realized assignment gives the observed outcome \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}:=Y_i(Z)\).

nl.statement: \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B):=\{(G_n,c):G_n\in\mathcal G_{n,d},\ c\in\mathcal C_{n,d,\beta}(B)\}\), where \(\mathcal G_{n,d}\) and \(\mathcal C_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) are the classes in \({\rm def:graph-class}\) and \({\rm def:coefficient-class}\), respectively.
nl.frozen_body:
Under \cref{obj:ass:bounded-degree,obj:ass:low-order,obj:ass:bounded-coefficient-mass}, with coefficient schedules supported on the in-neighborhoods in the sense that \(c_{i,S}=0\) whenever \(S\not\subseteq N_i\), define
\[
\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)
:=
\left\{
(G_n,c):
G_n\in\mathcal G_{n,d},\ 
c\in\mathcal C_{n,d,\beta}(B)
\right\}.
\]

review.note: The flattened structure is mathematically equivalent to a GraphClass paired with a CoeffClass for its edge relation, with exactly the bounded-degree, low-order, neighborhood-support, and coefficient-mass clauses.

Unfolding bernoulliContrast, effBeta, and nbhdB gives the displayed centered SNIPE sum; truncating at min β |N_i| is equivalent to the paper's min β d upper limit because all larger-cardinality subsets of N_i contribute an empty sum.

nl.statement: \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}:=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V_n}Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}g_{i,\beta,p}(Z)\) and \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{up}}:=\Pi_{[-B,B]}(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}})\), where \(\Pi_{[-B,B]}\) is Euclidean projection.
nl.frozen_body:
For each unit \(i\in V_n\), the observed outcome under the realized assignment is
\[
Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}:=Y_i(Z).
\]
The unprojected SNIPE estimator is
\[
\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}
:=
\frac{1}{n}
\sum_{i\in V_n}
Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}\,g_{i,\beta,p}(Z).
\]
The projected SNIPE estimator is
\[
\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{up}}
:=
\Pi_{[-B,B]}
\left(
\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}
\right),
\]
where \(\Pi_{[-B,B]}\) is Euclidean projection onto \([-B,B]\).

review.note: Unfolding the bundle, snipeEstimator is exactly card(V)⁻¹ times the sum of observed outcomes against the centered SNIPE score, and snipeClipped applies max(-B,min(B,x)), the Euclidean projection onto [-B,B] under the standing B≥0 setup.

nl.statement: \(R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B):=\inf_{\widehat\tau_n}\sup_{(G_n,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}\mathbb E_Z[(\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n)^2]\), where \(\widehat\tau_n\) is measurable in \((G_n,Z,\{Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}:i\in V_n\})\).
nl.frozen_body:
The finite-population all-treated-versus-all-control effect is
\[
\tau_n:=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i\in V_n}\bigl(Y_i(\mathbf 1)-Y_i(\mathbf 0)\bigr),
\]
where \(\mathbf 1\) and \(\mathbf 0\) denote the all-one and all-zero assignments. The minimax risk is
\[
R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B)
:=
\inf_{\widehat\tau_n}
\sup_{(G_n,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E_Z
\left[
\left(
\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n
\right)^2
\right].
\]

There are \(0<c_{\beta,p}\le C_{\beta,p}<\infty\) such that \[c_{\beta,p}B^2\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d\binom{d}{k_\star}}{n}\right\}\le R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B)\le\sup_{(G_n,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}\mathbb E_Z[(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{up}}-\tau_n)^2]\le C_{\beta,p}B^2\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d\binom{d}{k_\star}}{n}\right\}.\] In the nonsaturated regime \(d\binom{d}{k_\star}/n\lesssim_{\beta,p}1\), unclipped SNIPE attains the same rate. The upper bound uses \(A_i=\sum_{r=1}^{\min\{\beta,|N_i|\}}\binom{|N_i|}{r}\Delta_r(p)^2/[p(1-p)]^r\le A_d\) and the single-out-degree overlap count. For \(B>0\) and \(d\ge1\), the block mixtures have TTE separation \(2\rho\delta\) and squared Hellinger distance at most \(4\pi^2m\delta^2/(B^2A_d)\); since \(1/2\le\rho\le1\) and \(A_d/m=(dA_d/n)/\rho\), this yields the stated lower branch without a divisibility condition.
nl.frozen_body:
Fix an interaction order \(\beta\in\mathbb N\) and an assignment probability \(p\in\mathbb R\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Order.)} \(1\le \beta\).
\item \textbf{(Design probability.)} \(0<p<1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exist constants \(c_{\beta,p},C_{\beta,p}\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
0<c_{\beta,p}\le C_{\beta,p}.
\]
For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) and \(B\in\mathbb R\) satisfying \(1\le n\), \(d\le n\), and \(0\le B\), with \(k_\star(d,\beta,p)\) as in \cref{obj:def:exposed-order} and \(R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B)\) as in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}, the following hold:
\[
c_{\beta,p}B^2
\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}}{n}\right\}
\le
R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B).
\]
Moreover,
\[
R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B)
\le
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E_Z\!\left[
\left(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{up}}-\tau_n\right)^2
\right]
\le
C_{\beta,p}B^2
\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}}{n}\right\},
\]
where \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) is the model class in \cref{obj:def:model-class} and \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{up}}\) is SNIPE projected to \([-B,B]\). The unprojected SNIPE estimator also satisfies
\[
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E_Z\!\left[
\left(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n\right)^2
\right]
\le
C_{\beta,p}B^2
\frac{d\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}}{n}.
\]

For every \((G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) and unit \(i\), writing \(N_i=\{j:(j,i)\in G\}\),
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{\min\{\beta,|N_i|\}}
\binom{|N_i|}{r}
\frac{\Delta_r(p)^2}{\{p(1-p)\}^r}
\le
A_d,
\]
where
\[
A_d
=
\sum_{r=1}^{\min\{\beta,d\}}
\binom{d}{r}
\frac{\Delta_r(p)^2}{\{p(1-p)\}^r}.
\]
For every \((G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\), every \(r\in\mathbb N\), and every unit \(i\), if \(1\le r\), then
\[
\sum_{\ell\in V_n}
\binom{|N_i\cap N_\ell|}{r}
=
\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq N_i\\ |S|=r}}
\#\{\ell\in V_n:S\subseteq N_\ell\}
\le
d\binom{|N_i|}{r}
\le
d\binom{d}{r}.
\]

Finally, if \(0<B\) and \(1\le d\), let
\[
m=\left\lfloor\frac{n}{d}\right\rfloor,
\qquad
\rho=\frac{md}{n},
\qquad
\delta=\delta(n,d,\beta,B,p).
\]
For every \(U:\{1,\ldots,m\}\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(|U_b|\le B/2\) for all \(b\), there are models \(M_+\) and \(M_-\) in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) whose graph is the complete \(d\)-block graph, whose coefficient schedules are the corresponding block schedules with signs \(+1\) and \(-1\), and whose total treatment effects obey
\[
\tau_n(M_+)=\rho\delta,
\qquad
\tau_n(M_-)=-\rho\delta.
\]
The two block-prior densities with signs \(+1\) and \(-1\), relative to the block dominating measure, satisfy
\[
H^2(\Pi_+,\Pi_-)
\le
\frac{4\pi^2m\delta^2}{B^2A_d}.
\]
The active fraction and block energy satisfy
\[
\frac12\le \rho\le 1,
\qquad
\frac{A_d}{m}
=
\frac{dA_d/n}{\rho}.
\]

nl.statement:
Fix \(\beta\ge1\), \(p\in(0,1)\), and \(B>0\). For every index \(t\), let \(n_t\) and \(d_t\) be positive integers such that \(d_t\mid n_t\), write \(m_t:=n_t/d_t\), and let \(G_t\) be the fixed directed graph that is the disjoint union of \(m_t\) complete directed blocks \(V_b\) of size \(d_t\), including all self-loops. Then, for every \(t\),
\[
R_t^{\mathrm{loc,lin}}=\frac{B^2A_{d_t}}{m_t}=\frac{B^2d_tA_{d_t}}{n_t}.
\]
In particular, \(R_t^{\mathrm{loc,lin}}/(B^2d_tA_{d_t}/n_t)=1\) for every \(t\). More precisely, put \(Z_S:=\prod_{j\in S}Z_j\) and \(Z_b:=(Z_j)_{j\in V_b}\), and for every block \(V_b\) define
\[
\Psi_{b,t}(w):=\max_{\substack{(\varepsilon_i,S_i)_{i\in V_b}\\\varepsilon_i\in\{-1,1\},\ S_i\subseteq V_b,\ |S_i|\le\bar\beta_{d_t}}}
\mathbb E_Z\!\left[\left(\sum_{i\in V_b}\varepsilon_i\{w_{i,t}(Z_b)Z_{S_i}-\mathbf1(S_i\ne\varnothing)\}\right)^2\right].
\]
Then, for every \(t\),
\[
\sup_{c\in\mathcal M_t(G_t)}\mathbb E_Z[(\widehat\tau_{w,t}-\tau_{n_t})^2]
=\frac{B^2}{n_t^2}\sum_{b=1}^{m_t}\Psi_{b,t}(w),
\qquad
\Psi_{b,t}(w)\ge d_t^2A_{d_t}.
\]
A sequence in \(\mathcal E_t^{\mathrm{loc,lin}}\) is asymptotically minimax if and only if
\[
\frac{1}{m_td_t^2A_{d_t}}\sum_{b=1}^{m_t}\{\Psi_{b,t}(w)-d_t^2A_{d_t}\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The condition
\[
\frac{1}{n_tA_{d_t}}\sum_{i\in V_{n_t}}\mathbb E_Z[(w_{i,t}(Z_{b(i)})-g_{d_t}(Z_{b(i)}))^2]\longrightarrow0
\]
is sufficient for asymptotic minimaxity. Suppose in addition that \(d_t\to\infty\). This sufficient condition is not necessary, even up to relabeling coordinates within blocks. There are asymptotically minimax weights for which the last display equals \(2\) for every sufficiently large \(t\).

nl.statement:
Fix \(\beta\ge1\), \(p\in(0,1)\), \(B\ge0\), integers \(n\ge1\), and \(0\le d\le n\). The coefficient-mass model is contained in the uniformly bounded-outcome model, and the inclusion is strict whenever \(B>0\) and \(d\ge1\). There are \(0<c_{\beta,p}\le C_{\beta,p}<\infty\) such that
\[
c_{\beta,p}B^2\min\!\left\{1,\frac{dA_d}{n}\right\}
\le R_{n,\ell_1}^\star(d,\beta,p,B)=R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B)
\le R_{n,\infty}^\star(d,\beta,p,B)
\le \sup_{(G_n,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)}
\mathbb E_Z[(\widehat\tau_{n,\infty}^{\mathrm{up}}-\tau_n)^2]
\le C_{\beta,p}B^2\min\!\left\{1,\frac{dA_d}{n}\right\}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\sup_{(G_n,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E_Z[(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{up}}-\tau_n)^2]
\le C_{\beta,p}B^2\min\!\left\{1,\frac{dA_d}{n}\right\},
\]
and on either model class unclipped SNIPE is design-unbiased and has worst-case mean squared error at most \(B^2dA_d/n\). For every \(0\le d\le n\), \(dA_d\asymp_{\beta,p}d\binom d{k_\star}\), so both minimax risks are also \(\asymp_{\beta,p}B^2\min\{1,d\binom d{k_\star}/n\}\), and unclipped SNIPE attains the nonsaturated branch. If \(1\le d\le n\) and \(d\mid n\), put \(m=n/d\) and take the disjoint union of \(m\) complete directed \(d\)-blocks, including loops. Then canonical unclipped SNIPE has the exact global worst-case risk on both classes,
\[
\sup_{(G_n,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}\mathbb E_Z[(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n)^2]
=\sup_{(G_n,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)}\mathbb E_Z[(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n)^2]
=\frac{B^2A_d}{m}=\frac{B^2dA_d}{n},
\]
so the constant one in the global unclipped variance bound is sharp. The upper-bound calculation uses
\[
A_i=\sum_{r=1}^{\min\{\beta,|N_i|\}}\binom{|N_i|}{r}\frac{\Delta_r(p)^2}{[p(1-p)]^r}\le A_d
\]
and charges out-degree only once. For \(B>0\) and \(d\ge1\), the block mixtures in \({\rm def:block-family}\) lie in the smaller class, have TTE separation \(2\rho\delta\), and have squared Hellinger distance at most \(4\pi^2m\delta^2/(B^2A_d)\); furthermore \(1/2\le\rho\le1\) and \(A_d/m=(dA_d/n)/\rho\).

Fix an interaction order \(\beta\ge 1\) and a treatment probability \(p\in(0,1)\).  Then there are constants \(c_{\beta,p}\) and \(C_{\beta,p}\) such that \(0<c_{\beta,p}\le C_{\beta,p}\) and the following statements hold for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), every \(B\in\mathbb R\), and every finite design \(D\) on \(\{0,1\}^{V_n}\) satisfying the itemized conditions:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Population and degree.)} The population has size \(n\ge1\), \(V_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and the degree index satisfies \(d\le n\).
\item \textbf{(Radius.)} The radius satisfies \(B\ge0\).
\item \textbf{(Design.)} The design \(D\) is the product Bernoulli design with common treatment probability \(p\), as in \cref{obj:ass:bernoulli-design}.
\end{itemize}
Let
\[
A_d
=
\sum_{r=1}^{\bar\beta_d}
\binom{d}{r}
\frac{\Delta_r(p)^2}{\{p(1-p)\}^r},
\]
with \(\bar\beta_d\) and \(k_\star(d,\beta,p)\) as in \cref{obj:def:exposed-order}.  The coefficient-mass model \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) of \cref{obj:def:model-class} is contained in the uniformly bounded-outcome model \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)\) of \cref{obj:def:bounded-outcome-model-class}.  If \(B>0\) and \(d\ge1\), this inclusion is strict: some graph and bounded-outcome coefficient schedule in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)\) has no realization with the same graph and coefficient schedule in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\).

The minimax risks of \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk} satisfy
\[
c_{\beta,p} B^2
\min\!\left\{1,\frac{dA_d}{n}\right\}
\le
R_{n,\ell_1}^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B)
=
R_n^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B)
\le
R_{n,\infty}^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B).
\]
For the bounded-outcome clipped SNIPE estimator \(\widehat\tau_{n,\infty}^{\mathrm{up}}\) of \cref{obj:def:bounded-outcome-clipped-snipe},
\[
R_{n,\infty}^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B)
\le
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)}
\mathbb E_D\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_{n,\infty}^{\mathrm{up}}-\tau_n(G,c)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
C_{\beta,p} B^2
\min\!\left\{1,\frac{dA_d}{n}\right\}.
\]
The coefficient-class clipped SNIPE estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{up}}\) also satisfies
\[
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E_D\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{up}}-\tau_n(G,c)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
C_{\beta,p} B^2
\min\!\left\{1,\frac{dA_d}{n}\right\}.
\]

For every \((G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\), the unprojected SNIPE estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}\) is \(D\)-unbiased for \(\tau_n(G,c)\).  The same \(D\)-unbiasedness holds for every \((G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)\).  Its worst-case mean squared error obeys
\[
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E_D\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n(G,c)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\frac{B^2 d A_d}{n},
\]
and
\[
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)}
\mathbb E_D\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n(G,c)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\frac{B^2 d A_d}{n}.
\]
For every unit \(i\), on both \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) and \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)\), the local score energy is at most \(A_d\).

The complete-block energy is comparable to the exposed binomial term:
\[
c_{\beta,p}\, d\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}
\le
dA_d
\le
C_{\beta,p}\, d\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}.
\]

If \(d\ge1\) and \(d\mid n\), let \(m=n/d\) and let the graph be the disjoint union of \(m\) complete directed \(d\)-blocks, including loops.  Then canonical unprojected SNIPE has exact worst-case risk on the fixed block graph and globally on both classes:
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\text{ on the fixed block graph}}
\mathbb E_D\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n\bigr)^2
\right]
=
\frac{B^2A_d}{m},
\]
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)\text{ on the fixed block graph}}
\mathbb E_D\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n\bigr)^2
\right]
=
\frac{B^2A_d}{m},
\]
and
\[
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E_D\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n(G,c)\bigr)^2
\right]
=
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)}
\mathbb E_D\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n(G,c)\bigr)^2
\right]
=
\frac{B^2A_d}{m}
=
\frac{B^2dA_d}{n}.
\]

If \(B>0\) and \(d\ge1\), put
\[
m=\bigl\lfloor n/d\bigr\rfloor,
\qquad
\rho=\frac{md}{n},
\qquad
\delta=\delta(n,d,\beta,B,p)\ \text{ as in \cref{obj:def:block-family}}.
\]
For every vector \(U=(U_b)_{b=1}^m\) with \(|U_b|\le B/2\) for all \(b\), there are two coefficient-mass models on the block graph, with signs \(+1\) and \(-1\), whose coefficient schedules are the corresponding block schedules and whose total treatment effects are
\[
\tau_n^{+}=\rho\delta,
\qquad
\tau_n^{-}=-\rho\delta.
\]
For the two associated block priors \(\Pi_+\) and \(\Pi_-\),
\[
H^2(\Pi_+,\Pi_-)
\le
\frac{4\pi^2 m\delta^2}{B^2A_d},
\]
and the active share satisfies
\[
\frac12\le \rho\le 1,
\qquad
\frac{A_d}{m}
=
\frac{dA_d/n}{\rho}.
\]

Fix \(n\ge1\), \(1\le d\le n\), \(\beta\ge1\), \(B\ge0\), and \(p=1/2\). Then
\[
\Delta_r(1/2)=\begin{cases}2^{1-r},&r\text{ odd},\\0,&r\text{ even},\end{cases}
\qquad
A_d=4\sum_{\substack{1\le r\le\min\{\beta,d\}\\r\text{ odd}}}\binom dr.
\]
Consequently \(k_\star\) is the largest odd integer no greater than \(\min\{\beta,d\}\). For \(\beta=1\), \(A_d=4d\) and
\[
R_n^\star(d,1,1/2,B)=R_{n,\ell_1}^\star(d,1,1/2,B)
\asymp R_{n,\infty}^\star(d,1,1/2,B)
\asymp B^2\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n}\right\}.
\]
If additionally \(d\mid n\), canonical unclipped SNIPE has exact worst-case mean squared error \(4B^2d^2/n\) on both model classes.

For the fair-coin design \(p=1/2\), the following two conclusions hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Exact fair-coin contrasts.)} For every \(n,d,\beta\in\mathbb N\) and \(B\in\mathbb R\) with \(n\ge 1\), \(d\ge 1\), \(d\le n\), \(\beta\ge 1\), and \(B\ge 0\), the Bernoulli contrast coefficients satisfy, for every \(r\ge 1\),
\[
\Delta_r(1/2)
=
\begin{cases}
2^{1-r}, & r \text{ odd},\\
0, & r \text{ even}.
\end{cases}
\]
Consequently the complete-block score energy at interaction order \(\beta\) is
\[
A_d
=
4\sum_{\substack{1\le r\le \bar\beta_d\\ r\ \mathrm{odd}}}\binom dr,
\qquad
\bar\beta_d=\min\{\beta,d\},
\]
and the exposed order \(k_\star(d,\beta,1/2)\) from \cref{obj:def:exposed-order} is the largest odd integer at most \(\bar\beta_d\), with value \(0\) when no such odd integer exists.

\item \textbf{(First-order frontier.)} There exist constants \(c_{\mathrm{lower}},c_{\mathrm{upper}}\in\mathbb R\) with
\[
0<c_{\mathrm{lower}}\le c_{\mathrm{upper}}
\]
such that, for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) and \(B\in\mathbb R\) with \(n\ge 1\), \(d\ge 1\), \(d\le n\), and \(B\ge 0\), the order-one energy is
\[
A_d=4d,
\]
and the minimax risks of \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk} satisfy
\[
c_{\mathrm{lower}}B^2\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n}\right\}
\le
R_n^\star(d,1,1/2,B),
\]
\[
R_n^\star(d,1,1/2,B)
=
R_{n,\ell_1}^\star(d,1,1/2,B)
\le
R_{n,\infty}^\star(d,1,1/2,B)
\le
c_{\mathrm{upper}}B^2\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n}\right\}.
\]
If additionally \(d\mid n\), then the unprojected SNIPE estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}\) has exact worst-case mean squared error
\[
\sup_{M\in\mathcal M_{n,d,1}(B)}
\mathbb E_{1/2,M}\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n\bigr)^2
\right]
=
\frac{4B^2d^2}{n},
\]
and, over the uniformly bounded-outcome class,
\[
\sup_{M\in\mathcal M_{n,d,1}^{\infty}(B)}
\mathbb E_{1/2,M}\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n\bigr)^2
\right]
=
\frac{4B^2d^2}{n}.
\]
\end{itemize}
